title: Australian Consumer Law (Competition and Consumer Act 2010, Schedule 2)
verification_notes: Sections 2, 18, 21, 23, 29, 50, 54, 64, 259 and 263 were checked on 2026-10-27 against compilation C2026C00405 (Compilation No. 167, 16 September 2026, Volume 4 holds Schedule 2) and the existing paraphrases of ss18, 21, 23, 29 and 50 match the text. Section 34, the consumer definition (s3), Crown application (CCA s2A) and penalties were not re-read, nor was the exclusion of private health insurance from the ASIC Act financial services protections. A compliance SME must confirm before reliance.
summary: The ACL is the general consumer protection law administered by the ACCC. Financial services consumer protections for general and life insurance sit in the ASIC Act instead, but private health insurance is not a financial product for those purposes, so misleading statements, unconscionable conduct and unfair terms by private health insurers and their agents are assessed under the ACL. Included here so private health findings cite the right regime.

clauses.section_name: Chapter 2, Part 2-1: Misleading or deceptive conduct
clauses.heading: Misleading or deceptive conduct
clauses.text: A person must not, in trade or commerce, engage in conduct that is misleading or deceptive or is likely to mislead or deceive.
clauses.notes: An agent's statement about what a health policy covers, or how much it costs, is conduct in trade or commerce. Remedies include injunctions, damages and corrective orders; there is no pecuniary penalty under s18 itself.

clauses.heading: Unconscionable conduct in connection with goods or services
clauses.text: A person must not, in trade or commerce, engage in conduct that is unconscionable in connection with supplying or acquiring services, considering factors such as relative bargaining strength, undue pressure and the customer's circumstances.
clauses.notes: Pressure tactics or exploiting a vulnerable member (for example during bereavement or illness) can engage this provision. Civil penalties apply.

clauses.heading: Unfair terms of consumer contracts and small business contracts
clauses.text: An unfair term of a standard form consumer or small business contract is void, and proposing or relying on such a term can attract civil penalties.
clauses.notes: Relevant to fund rules and policy terms an agent quotes; the agent should not assert a term that a court could find unfair as if it were settled.

clauses.heading: False or misleading representations about goods or services
clauses.text: A person must not, in trade or commerce, make a false or misleading representation about matters including the standard, quality or price of services, or the existence or effect of any condition, warranty, guarantee, right or remedy.
clauses.notes: Telling a member that extras pay for GP visits, that a waiting period is waived, or that premiums will never rise can be a false representation about the services or their price. Civil penalties apply.

clauses.heading: Misleading conduct as to the nature of services
clauses.text: A person must not, in trade or commerce, engage in conduct that is liable to mislead the public about the nature, characteristics, suitability for purpose or quantity of services.
clauses.notes: Applies to agent statements describing what a hospital or extras product includes.

clauses.heading: Harassment and coercion
clauses.text: A person must not use physical force, undue harassment or coercion in connection with supplying services or collecting payment for them.
clauses.notes: Relevant to automated premium arrears and retention conversations.

clauses.heading: Trade or commerce
clauses.text: Trade or commerce means trade or commerce within Australia or between Australia and places outside Australia, and includes any business or professional activity, whether or not carried on for profit. Most ACL prohibitions apply only to conduct in trade or commerce.
clauses.notes: Scope test for most ACL prohibitions.

clauses.heading: Guarantee as to acceptable quality
clauses.text: Goods supplied to a consumer in trade or commerce (other than by auction) come with a guarantee that they are of acceptable quality: fit for all their usual purposes, acceptable in appearance and finish, free from defects, safe and durable, as a reasonable consumer would regard as acceptable.
clauses.notes: An agent that denies a repair, replacement or refund for faulty goods engages this guarantee.

clauses.heading: Guarantees cannot be excluded
clauses.text: A contract term is void to the extent it purports to exclude, restrict or modify the consumer guarantees, the application of the guarantee provisions, or a consumer's rights or remedies for their breach.
clauses.notes: 'No refunds' or 'warranty only through the manufacturer' statements engage s64 and s29(1)(m).

clauses.heading: Remedies for failure of a consumer guarantee
clauses.text: If a supplier fails to comply with a consumer guarantee, the consumer may require a remedy within a reasonable time. For a major failure the consumer may reject the goods or seek compensation for reduced value, whether or not the goods are in their original packaging (s259(2), (3), (7)). On rejection the supplier must refund or replace as the consumer chooses, and cannot satisfy a refund by offering goods instead, such as store credit (s263(4), (5)).
clauses.notes: Includes s263(4) and (5): a refund cannot be replaced with store credit.
